newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia bank SKB up 33 pct on strong GDR demand.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia bank SKB up 33 pct on strong GDR demand.

text.p: Slovenian bank SKB jumped 32.8 percent in early Friday trade after the bank said there was strong demand for its global depository receipts (GDR) prior to their listing on the London bourse.
"Demand for the first GDR issue was 25 times higher than bid," Polona Vagaja a spokeswoman of SKB told Reuters.
The bank's GDRs will be listed on the London Stock Exchange in mid February. GDRs will represent up to 29 percent of SKB's capital and one share will be worth 20 GDRs.
Last week the Bank of Slovenia approved SKB's listing abroad by giving the green light to increase the maximum foreign shareholding in SKB to 49 percent from 30 percent.
* The SBI index at 1125 GMT jumped 4.74 percent to 1,592.02.
* SKB was the most active and the biggest gainer, jumping 32.8 percent to 78,000 tolars on volume of 10,417 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
